title: add benchmark-lab performance suites, profiling baselines, representative runners, and reporting pipeline
author: Ethan Park
description:
This PR adds a consolidated set of performance test suites, profiling baselines, representative workload runners, and an end-to-end reporting pipeline for the benchmark-lab. Motivation: standardize how we collect, store, and report runtime performance and memory profiles for both adaptive-batching and cold-start scenarios so that teams can compare model variants and infra configurations reproducibly. Primary changes: 1) new pytest-based performance test harness (benchlab/tests/perf/) with parametrized workloads to exercise adaptive batching, KV-cache warm/cold, and mixed request sizes; 2) profiling baselines (benchlab/profiling/baselines/) containing canonical traces and memory usage snapshots for representative models and sequence lengths; 3) representative workload runners (benchlab/runners/) for GPU/CPU variants with k8s job manifests and local dev runner wrappers; 4) reporting pipeline (benchlab/reporting/) implemented as an Airflow DAG (and a minimal standalone runner) that ingests runner output, normalizes metrics, writes summary rows to BigQuery, and pushes timeseries to the observability-pack dashboards. Checklists:
- [x] Add perf test harness and testcases
- [x] Add profiling baselines and baseline ingestion code
- [x] Add representative runners and k8s job templates
- [x] Add Airflow DAG + reporting transformer + CI smoke job
- [x] Add docs and Quickstart for running locally and on CI
Notes: The description string below includes high-level rationale for the reporting schema and the canonical runner configs. This PR intentionally avoids large binary artifacts in the tree; baselines are stored as compressed artifacts uploaded to the benchmark S3 bucket by the release job (see benchlab/deploy/upload_baselines.sh).
commits_summary: 6 commits — initial harness and tests; add profiling baseline schema and uploader; add k8s runner templates + local wrapper; implement reporting transformer + airflow DAG; CI smoke tests and fixtures; docs and quickstart. Commits are small and focused to keep reviewable diffs; I squashed minor fixups before merging.
review_comments: Ava Chen (2025-11-04): Nice consolidation — can you add a test that asserts the runner times are captured when KV cache is hot vs cold? This is important for the adaptive-batching numbers to be comparable.
Ethan Park (2025-11-04): Added a parametrized test in benchlab/tests/perf/test_cold_start.py to cover hot/cold KV cache. Also added fixtures to simulate warmup sequences.
Marco Ruiz (2025-11-05): Observability push looks fine but please make the BigQuery insert idempotent — we should avoid duplicates when the DAG is retried.
Ethan Park (2025-11-05): Updated bigquery_client to use insertAll with a dedup key (runner_run_id) and added a unit test for retry behavior.
Priya Nandakumar (2025-11-06): Can we reduce the default runner concurrency in the k8s template? 16 concurrent jobs burned through our dev quota during tests. Suggest default 4.
Ethan Park (2025-11-06): Lowered default concurrency to 4 and added explicit resource requests/limits to avoid noisy neighbor issues. Also added docs note about quota guidance.
Ava Chen (2025-11-07): CI flaky on macOS-based smoke job — looks like pathing for the local runner script. Please make run.sh POSIX-compliant.
Ethan Park (2025-11-07): Fixed run.sh to be POSIX-compliant and added a CI matrix entry for the smoke runner that exercises the local runner on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest (lightweight).
Marco Ruiz (2025-11-09): Approving — tests green locally and BigQuery dedupe looks good. Recommend follow-up to add historical dashboarding for model-to-model comparisons.
Priya Nandakumar (2025-11-09): Approving — loader and reporting DAG are well documented. Good to merge once CI finishes the final airflow integration job.
